title: Outsourcing human resources

match.reason: No point in the bank covers outsourcing human resource tasks; the nearest points deal with the internal environment or management roles, not with using outside firms for payroll, recruitment or training.

draft.title: Outsourcing human resources
card: Outsourcing means paying an outside firm to do a task instead of doing it inside the business.
HR tasks often outsourced include payroll, recruitment and training. The outside firm may be in Australia or overseas.
it can save costs, as the business does not need its own staff or systems for the task. It can also use the skills of specialists.
the business has less control over how the task is done, and may have less contact with its own staff. Quality may also vary.
draft.remember: Outsourcing HR can cut costs but the business gives up some control.

a.q: A business pays an outside firm to run its payroll. What is a likely disadvantage?
opts: Less control over how the payroll task is done
Higher costs from hiring extra payroll staff
Slower growth in sales because of the change
Less need for any planning of staffing
a.why: Handing a task to an outside firm means the business has less say in how it is done. Hiring extra payroll staff would be a cost of doing the task in-house, not of outsourcing it.
a.clue: Think about who now decides how the task is done.

b.q: Ken's small plumbing firm in Geelong hires a recruitment agency to find a new apprentice, rather than advertising itself. What is the most likely benefit?
opts: Saved time and costs, as the agency has hiring expertise
Full control over how candidates are screened
Closer contact between Ken and every applicant
No fee, as agencies work without charge
b.why: Agencies specialise in hiring, so Ken saves time and can avoid building his own system. Full control is wrong because screening is done by the agency, which is the trade-off of outsourcing.
b.clue: Which benefit comes from using a specialist?

a.best: Less control over how the payroll task is done

b.best: Saved time and costs, as the agency has hiring expertise

problems.detail: The right option is clearly the longest and the most detailed (10 words against about 6–7 for the others), so a student could pick it without knowing the idea.

'Saved ... costs' is stated flatly. A recruitment agency charges fees that can be more than a small firm would spend advertising the job itself. The card only says outsourcing 'can' save costs, and it does not teach that it saves time. Wording such as 'May save time, as the agency has hiring expertise' would be safer.

check.summary: The card and question a are sound. In question b the right option is noticeably longer than the others, and it says outright that using an agency saves costs, which may not hold for a small firm paying agency fees.
